summary: Claus Oetke worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD and habilitation at the University of Hamburg, later teaching there (~1973–1989) and heading Indology at Stockholm University (1993–2014), alongside posts at Vienna and Kiel.

Claus Vogel specialized in Indology and Tibetology. He completed his PhD and habilitation at the University of Marburg, also studying at Deccan College. His career included professorships at Marburg, the University of Göttingen, and the University of Bonn (1976–1998).
Clemency Montelle is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She has held posts at the University of Canterbury, including Associate Professor in 2007 and an appointment spanning 2020–2025.

Clemens a Jesu was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Urban College until 1756. He served in the Archdiocese of Verapoly (~1757–1782) and became General Vicar of the Malabar Mission in 1774.

Clements Markham worked in history, archaeology, and Tibetology, having studied at Cheam School and Westminster School. He served as Secretary and President of both the Hakluyt Society and the Royal Geographical Society, and as Assistant Secretary at the India Office.
Clinton B. Seely was an Indologist who held posts at the University of Chicago, attested in 2007 and in 2026 as Professor, Emeritus of South Asian Languages and Civilizations.

Clyde Kluckhohn studied at Princeton, Wisconsin-Madison, Corpus Christi College (Oxford), Vienna, and Harvard. He held academic posts at the University of New Mexico (~1932–1934) and Harvard University (~1935–1960).

Colette Caillat specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying under Walther Schubring, Louis Renou, and Jules Bloch. She held posts at CNRS, the University of Lyon, the Sorbonne, the Institut de Civilisation Indienne, and the Institut de France.

Colette Sciberras specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied at Durham University under doctoral supervisors David E. Cooper and Simon P. James, and also studied with traditional teachers Yungdrung Nyima and Chamtrul Rinpoche.
Colin Leslie Dean is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies who studied under supervisors Peter Fenner and Purushottama Bilimoria.

Colin Mackenzie was an Indologist and surveyor educated at Dollar Academy. His appointments included engineer in the Madras Engineer Group (1786), Surveyor-General of Madras at the University of Madras (1807), and Surveyor General of the Survey of India (1810–1815).
Colin Turnbull was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He completed his studies at Westminster School (~1938–1942), Magdalen College (~1942–1947), and Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1951).

Collett Cox is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University and studied at the University of Tokyo and Ryukoku University. In 1985, she became a professor at the University of Washington.

Congjun Long works in the fields of computational linguistics and Tibetology. Long has held academic posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Conor Roddy works in philosophy and Indology. Roddy earned a PhD from the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011) under Kathleen Higgins, having also studied under William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.

Conrad Bursian was a scholar of history and archaeology who studied at Thomasschule, Leipzig, and Berlin. He held posts at Leipzig, Tübingen (~1861–1864), Zurich (~1864–1869), Jena (~1869–1874), and Munich (~1874–1883).
Conrad M. Arensberg studied at Harvard University (~1927–1934) and later held an academic post at Columbia University (~1952–1979).

Constance E. Kassor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed degrees at Smith College and Emory University, and has held posts at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, Smith College, and Lawrence University.
Constance Powell Chin works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. Chin studied under Christian Luczanits and earned a master's degree from San Jose State University in 2012.

Constant Chounavel worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the Major Seminary of Saint-Dié (~1845–1850) and later held posts in the Roman Catholic Diocese of Jaffna (1852–1883) and as pastor at St. Lucia's Cathedral.
